subject: Hosted evaluation: quickstart steps, endpoints & rate limits
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@finsight.ai>, Alex Chen <alex@finsight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation: quickstart steps, endpoints & rate limits

Hi Olivia / Alex — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a hosted quickstart that matches your constraints.

Call highlights:
- You want to validate our hosted API for inference (chat + streaming) for a conversational summarization flow.
- Target production-ish traffic: initial 15k users/month, expected spiky peaks ~120 RPS for short bursts (2–3s), steady-state 20–40 RPS.
- Latency target: 200–400ms p50 token generation; high-percentile sensitivity for UI flows.
- Primary concern: data residency and token-level visibility for cost analysis.

Our proposed quickstart deliverables:
1) Sandbox endpoints (read-only test keys) mapped to the same route names you will use in prod. We will provision 1 sandbox endpoint per model variant.
2) Default rate caps in sandbox: 200 QPS with an initial ramp plan to 500 QPS across 7 days if metrics look healthy. Ops will handle temporary burst windows.
3) Prefix/KV caching enabled for session affinity (saves tokens on repeated prompts). We will include guidance for cache keys.
4) Short test prompt set + perf script you can run from your infra to validate p50/p95.

Requests for you to confirm (helps us size the hosted trial):
- Confirm preferred region (we proposed us-west).
- Estimated avg tokens per request (prompt + expected generation).
- Any required IP allowlist / corporate network egress constraints.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (quick operations checklist) — I attached the short ops guide. Also please attach a simple traffic sketch (requests/min by hour) if you have it.

Can you confirm the three bullets above and share the traffic sketch? Once we have that Marissa & Ben will provision the sandbox and I’ll send credentials + a one-hour runbook session.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0122

From: Olivia Park <olivia@finsight.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@finsight.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: quickstart steps, endpoints & rate limits

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. Real quick answers inline below.

- Region: us-west is fine for our initial evaluation.
- Avg tokens/request: ~850 tokens (300 prompt + ~550 generation) for the longer flows; smaller flows ~200 tokens.
- IP allowlist: we can provide a CIDR range for our office egress. No private connectivity required for the first trial.

A few questions from our side:
1) Can you confirm how prefix/KV caching interacts with streaming (do we see fewer tokens billed on repeat prompts)?
2) For the sandbox, can we get a temporary increase to 300 QPS for a 48-hour spike window during our internal load test next week?

Attached: finsight-traffic-profile.xlsx (hourly sketch + expected peaks).

Thanks — Olivia
Head of Platform, FinSight Analytics
olivia@finsight.ai

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Olivia’s responses and the attached traffic sketch. Action items:
- Marissa: please provision sandbox endpoints in us-west as described. Start with default caps 200 QPS but allow ops to temporarily bump to 300 QPS for a 48-hour test window next Wednesday-Thursday. We’ll record the spike.
- Ben: confirm prefix/KV caching behavior with streaming tokens — we should include a short note for Olivia on token accounting and a recommendation for cache-key strategy.

Attachments: finsight-traffic-profile.xlsx (from Olivia).

I’ll schedule a 30-minute ops handoff once the sandbox is provisioned.

Thanks — Vanessa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted evaluation: quickstart steps, endpoints & rate limits

Vanessa — got it. Quick operational answers:
- Sandbox provisioning: we can spin up 2 endpoint routes ("conversation-alpha" and "conversation-beta") in us-west within the day. Keys + a short onboarding note will go to Olivia.
- Rate caps: start 200 QPS per endpoint, can bump to 300 QPS for the 48-hour window (we'll set a timed policy). After successful test we can do a controlled ramp to 500 QPS over 7 days.
- Caching + streaming: prefix/KV cache reduces billed prompt tokens on repeated prefixes; streaming responses still bill generated tokens as usual. In practice you’ll see lower token volume for repeated prompts (saves on prompt tokens), but generation token billing is unchanged. I’ll draft a one-paragraph explanation for Olivia.
- Attachments and runbook: I uploaded a short ops checklist and rate policy snippet to the shared drive (link in thread metadata).

I’ll proceed with provisioning and will DM Ops on the timed bump for next Wednesday.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
